title: Costs and benefits of friendly boards during mergers and acquisitions
primary_theories: information exchange between CEO and board (Adams and Ferreira, 2007)

rival_explanations: outside representation (regulatory definition of board independence) captures the effect rather than social ties
outside representation (regulatory definition of board independence) rather than social ties drives the monitoring effect

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (mergers and acquisitions by publicly traded US bidders across all industries)

data_sources.name: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP)
